description:
FILED s470bp (Opus, 2026-09-05) from a probe written for #1188's guard file.
PRE-EXISTING and unchanged by #1188: both the fasl path and the text path
answer the same (wrong) thing, which is why the guard row was dropped and this
task written instead.

REPRODUCER (scratch/s470bp/probe-pcl.pl in the s470bp worktree):

    # CheckMod.pm
    package CheckMod;
    our $ran = 0;
    CHECK { $ran = 1 }
    sub ran { $ran }
    1;

    # main
    use CheckMod; print "ran=", CheckMod::ran(), "\n";

    perl 5.40.3   ran=1
    PCL           ran=0        (fasl path AND text path)

WHY.  `use` is a compile-time require, so perl registers the module's CHECK
block during the main program's COMPILATION and runs it at the end of that
compilation — hence ran=1.  A RUNTIME `require` is the other case: perl then
warns "Too late to run CHECK block" and does not run it.  PCL emits
`(p-CHECK …)`, whose expansion is `(eval-when (:load-toplevel) …)`; a module
is `load`ed (as text, or as a fasl built with *PCL-FASL-BUILD*), and CLHS
3.2.3.1 gives a source load only the :execute situation, so the block is
never reached.  PCL therefore answers perl's RUNTIME-require behaviour for
both spellings.

#1188 deliberately kept that: `%p-check-situations` returns (:execute) while a
module fasl is built, which compile-file DISCARDS, so the fasl-loaded module
behaves exactly like the source-loaded one.  Making the fasl run it (its
:load-toplevel would have) would have been a DIVERGENCE BETWEEN THE TWO PATHS
— worse than a shared wrong answer.

THE FIX has to distinguish the two require spellings, which PCL's emission
does not carry today: a compile-time `use` must run the module's CHECK/
UNITCHECK blocks at the end of the requiring unit's compile phase (PCL already
has that phase — `p-run-compile-phase-blocks`, and *p-compile-phase-done*
records the boundary), and a run-time `require` must announce "Too late to run
CHECK block" and not run them.  So: register the block at module load into
`*check-blocks*` (as a program's own CHECK does) whenever the load happens
before the boundary, and announce+drop after it.

SIZE: small, and it is a CORRECTNESS row, not a speed one.  Rare in CPAN
(CHECK/UNITCHECK in a module is unusual), which is why it has never been
noticed — but it is silent, and the announce half is rule 12's shape.


=== DONE (s507c, Opus 5.5, 2026-10-05) -- closed by #2690 ===
A module's CHECK/INIT blocks are now spliced onto the program's queues by the loader (%p-load-unit) while the main program compiles, and dropped after its boundary (a run-time require).  The reproducer here prints ran=1 (perl ran=1) on the text path and from the cached fasl; Pl/t/phase-units-01.t rows 6-9 guard it (module CHECK/INIT join the queues; UNITCHECK runs at the module's own boundary; a run-time require runs neither).  The CHECK emission is `(push (lambda …) *check-blocks*)` today, not the p-CHECK macro this task describes.  The "Too late to run CHECK block" WARNING is not emitted (warnings-gated, the #221 class).
subject: A CHECK/UNITCHECK block in a `use`d module never runs — perl runs it at the end of the requiring unit's compile phase (ran=1 vs PCL ran=0); PRE-EXISTING, both paths agree
